sanskrit: hiraṇyavarṇaṃ yaṃ garbham aditir daityanāśanam ekaṃ dvādaśadhā jajñe tasmai sūryātmane namaḥ
english: To him whom Aditi bore as a golden-hued embryo, destroyer of the Daityas, the one brought forth in twelvefold form—to him whose Self is the Sun, homage.

sanskrit: śukle devān pitṝn kṛṣṇe tarpayaty amṛtena yaḥ yaś ca rājā dvijātīnāṃ tasmai somātmane namaḥ
english: To him who in the bright fortnight gladdens the gods and in the dark fortnight the ancestors with the nectar, and who is king over the twice-born—to him whose Self is the Moon, homage.

sanskrit: mahatas tamasaḥ pāre puruṣaṃ jvalanadyutim yaṃ jñātvā mṛtyum atyeti tasmai jñeyātmane namaḥ
english: To the Person beyond the great darkness, shining with flame, whom having known a man transcends death—to him whose Self is the Knowable, homage.

sanskrit: yaṃ bṛhantaṃ bṛhaty ukthe yam agnau yaṃ mahādhvare yaṃ viprasaṃghā gāyanti tasmai vedātmane namaḥ
english: To him, the Vast, whom they hymn in the bṛhatī verse and in the recitation, in the fire and in the great sacrifice, whom assemblies of brahmins chant—to him whose Self is the Veda, homage.

sanskrit: ṛgyajuḥsāmadhāmānaṃ daśārdhahavirākṛtim yaṃ saptatantuṃ tanvanti tasmai yajñātmane namaḥ
english: To him whose abode is Ṛk, Yajus, and Sāman, whose form is the fivefold oblation, whom they extend as the seven-threaded rite—to him whose Self is the Sacrifice, homage.

sanskrit: yaḥ suparṇo yajur nāma chandogātras trivṛcchirāḥ rathaṃtarabṛhatyakṣas tasmai stotrātmane namaḥ
english: To him who is the fair-winged bird named the Yajus, whose body is the chant, whose head is the trivṛt hymn, whose eyes are the Rathaṃtara and Bṛhat sāmans—to him whose Self is the Praise-song, homage.

sanskrit: yaḥ sahasrasave satre jajñe viśvasṛjām ṛṣiḥ hiraṇyavarṇaḥ śakunis tasmai haṃsātmane namaḥ
english: To him who was born in the thousand-pressing session as the seer of the world's creators, a golden-hued bird—to him whose Self is the Swan, homage.

sanskrit: padāṅgaṃ saṃdhiparvāṇaṃ svaravyañjanalakṣaṇam yam āhur akṣaraṃ nityaṃ tasmai vāgātmane namaḥ
english: To him whose limbs are the words, whose joints are the junctures, marked by vowels and consonants, whom they call the eternal Imperishable Syllable—to him whose Self is Speech, homage.

sanskrit: yaś cinoti satāṃ setum ṛtenāmṛtayoninā dharmārthavyavahārāṅgais tasmai satyātmane namaḥ
english: To him who builds up the dike of the good with cosmic order, the womb of immortality, and with the limbs of dharma, purpose, and right conduct—to him whose Self is Truth, homage.

sanskrit: yaṃ pṛthagdharmacaraṇāḥ pṛthagdharmaphalaiṣiṇaḥ pṛthagdharmaiḥ samarcanti tasmai dharmātmane namaḥ
english: To him whom those who follow diverse duties, seeking the diverse fruits of duty, worship through their diverse observances—to him whose Self is Dharma, homage.

sanskrit: yaṃ taṃ vyaktastham avyaktaṃ vicinvanti maharṣayaḥ kṣetre kṣetrajñam āsīnaṃ tasmai kṣetrātmane namaḥ
english: To him, the Unmanifest abiding in the manifest, whom the great seers seek out, the Knower of the field seated within the field—to him whose Self is the Field, homage.

sanskrit: yaṃ dṛgātmānam ātmasthaṃ vṛtaṃ ṣoḍaśabhir guṇaiḥ prāhuḥ saptadaśaṃ sāṃkhyās tasmai sāṃkhyātmane namaḥ
english: To him whom the Sāṃkhyas declare to be the seeing Self, abiding in the self, encompassed by the sixteen constituents and reckoned the seventeenth—to him whose Self is Sāṃkhya, homage.

sanskrit: yaṃ vinidrā jitaśvāsāḥ sattvasthāḥ saṃyatendriyāḥ jyotiḥ paśyanti yuñjānās tasmai yogātmane namaḥ
english: To him whom the sleepless, who have mastered the breath, who are established in purity, with senses restrained, behold as a light while in meditation—to him whose Self is Yoga, homage.

sanskrit: apuṇyapuṇyoparame yaṃ punarbhavanirbhayāḥ śāntāḥ saṃnyāsino yānti tasmai mokṣātmane namaḥ
english: To him whom, when both demerit and merit have ceased, the tranquil renouncers, freed from fear of rebirth, attain—to him whose Self is Liberation, homage.

sanskrit: yo 'sau yugasahasrānte pradīptārcir vibhāvasuḥ saṃbhakṣayati bhūtāni tasmai ghorātmane namaḥ
english: To him who, at the close of a thousand ages, with blazing flame as the radiant fire, devours all beings—to him whose Self is the Terrible, homage.

sanskrit: saṃbhakṣya sarvabhūtāni kṛtvā caikārṇavaṃ jagat bālaḥ svapiti yaś caikas tasmai māyātmane namaḥ
english: To him who, having devoured all beings and made the world a single ocean, sleeps alone as a child—to him whose Self is Illusion, homage.

sanskrit: sahasraśirase tasmai puruṣāyāmitātmane catuḥsamudraparyāyayoganidrātmane namaḥ
english: To that thousand-headed Person of measureless Self, whose Self is the yoga-slumber that circles round the four oceans, homage.

sanskrit: ajasya nābhāv adhyekaṃ yasmin viśvaṃ pratiṣṭhitam puṣkaraṃ puṣkarākṣasya tasmai padmātmane namaḥ
english: To him, the lotus-eyed one, in whose single lotus rising from the navel of the Unborn the whole universe is established—to him whose Self is the Lotus, homage.

sanskrit: yasya keśeṣu jīmūtā nadyaḥ sarvāṅgasaṃdhiṣu kukṣau samudrāś catvāras tasmai toyātmane namaḥ
english: To him in whose hair are the rain-clouds, in the joints of whose every limb are the rivers, and in whose belly are the four oceans—to him whose Self is the Waters, homage.

sanskrit: yugeṣv āvartate yo 'ṃśair dinartvanayahāyanaiḥ sargapralayayoḥ kartā tasmai kālātmane namaḥ
english: To him who revolves through the ages by his portions—days, seasons, fortnights, and years—the maker of creation and dissolution—to him whose Self is Time, homage.

sanskrit: brahma vaktraṃ bhujau kṣatraṃ kṛtsnam ūrūdaraṃ viśaḥ pādau yasyāśritāḥ śūdrās tasmai varṇātmane namaḥ
english: To him whose mouth is the brahmins, whose arms are the warriors, whose whole thighs and belly are the commoners, and on whose feet the śūdras rest—to him whose Self is the social orders, homage.

sanskrit: yasyāgnir āsyaṃ dyaur mūrdhā khaṃ nābhiś caraṇau kṣitiḥ sūryaś cakṣur diśaḥ śrotre tasmai lokātmane namaḥ
english: To him whose mouth is Agni, whose head is the sky, whose navel is space, whose feet are the earth, whose eye is the Sun, and whose ears are the quarters—to him whose Self is the worlds, homage.

sanskrit: viṣaye vartamānānāṃ yaṃ taṃ vaiśeṣikair guṇaiḥ prāhur viṣayagoptāraṃ tasmai goptrātmane namaḥ
english: To him whom they declare, by the Vaiśeṣika categories, to be the guardian of the objects for those engaged amid sense-objects—to him whose Self is the Protector, homage.

sanskrit: annapānendhanamayo rasaprāṇavivardhanaḥ yo dhārayati bhūtāni tasmai prāṇātmane namaḥ
english: To him who, composed of food, drink, and fuel, increasing the sap and the vital breath, sustains all beings—to him whose Self is the Breath of Life, homage.

sanskrit: paraḥ kālāt paro yajñāt paraḥ sadasatoś ca yaḥ anādir ādir viśvasya tasmai viśvātmane namaḥ
english: To him who is beyond Time, beyond the sacrifice, beyond both being and non-being, beginningless yet the beginning of the universe—to him whose Self is the All, homage.

sanskrit: yo mohayati bhūtāni sneharāgānubandhanaiḥ sargasya rakṣaṇārthāya tasmai mohātmane namaḥ
english: To him who deludes living beings with the bonds of affection and passion, for the sake of preserving creation—to him whose Self is Delusion, homage.

sanskrit: ātmajñānam idaṃ jñānaṃ jñātvā pañcasv avasthitam yaṃ jñānino 'dhigacchanti tasmai jñānātmane namaḥ
english: To him whom the knowers reach, having known this self-knowledge, the knowledge abiding within the five—to him whose Self is Knowledge, homage.

sanskrit: aprameyaśarīrāya sarvato 'nantacakṣuṣe apāraparimeyāya tasmai cintyātmane namaḥ
english: To him of immeasurable body, with infinite eyes on every side, boundless and beyond all measure—to him whose Self is the Object of Contemplation, homage.

sanskrit: jaṭine daṇḍine nityaṃ lambodaraśarīriṇe kamaṇḍaluniṣaṅgāya tasmai brahmātmane namaḥ
english: To him with matted locks, bearing the staff, ever pot-bellied in form, girded with the water-pot—to him whose Self is Brahmā, homage.

sanskrit: śūline tridaśeśāya tryambakāya mahātmane bhasmadigdhordhvaliṅgāya tasmai rudrātmane namaḥ
english: To him who bears the trident, lord of the gods, the three-eyed great one, smeared with ashes, his liṅga upraised—to him whose Self is Rudra, homage.

sanskrit: pañcabhūtātmabhūtāya bhūtādinidhanātmane akrodhadrohamohāya tasmai śāntātmane namaḥ
english: To him who has become the Self of the five elements, the Self of the origin and end of beings, free from anger, malice, and delusion—to him whose Self is Peace, homage.

sanskrit: yasmin sarvaṃ yataḥ sarvaṃ yaḥ sarvaṃ sarvataś ca yaḥ yaś ca sarvamayo nityaṃ tasmai sarvātmane namaḥ
english: To him in whom is all, from whom is all, who is all, who is on every side, and who is eternally made of all—to him whose Self is the Whole, homage.

sanskrit: viśvakarman namas te 'stu viśvātman viśvasaṃbhava apavargo 'si bhūtānāṃ pañcānāṃ parataḥ sthitaḥ
english: O Maker of all, homage be to you, Self of all, source of all; you are the deliverance of beings, standing beyond the five elements.

sanskrit: namas te triṣu lokeṣu namas te paratastriṣu namas te dikṣu sarvāsu tvaṃ hi sarvaparāyaṇam
english: Homage to you in the three worlds, homage to you in the three beyond, homage to you in all the quarters—for you are the supreme refuge of all.

sanskrit: namas te bhagavan viṣṇo lokānāṃ prabhavāpyaya tvaṃ hi kartā hṛṣīkeśa saṃhartā cāparājitaḥ
english: Homage to you, Lord Viṣṇu, origin and dissolution of the worlds; for you, Hṛṣīkeśa, are the maker and the unconquered destroyer.

sanskrit: tena paśyāmi te divyān bhāvān hi triṣu vartmasu tac ca paśyāmi tattvena yat te rūpaṃ sanātanam
english: By that grace I behold your divine manifestations upon the three paths, and I behold in its very truth that eternal form of yours.

sanskrit: divaṃ te śirasā vyāptaṃ padbhyāṃ devī vasuṃdharā vikrameṇa trayo lokāḥ puruṣo 'si sanātanaḥ
english: By your head the heaven is pervaded, by your feet the goddess Earth, and by your stride the three worlds—you are the eternal Person.

sanskrit: atasīpuṣpasaṃkāśaṃ pītavāsasam acyutam ye namasyanti govindaṃ na teṣāṃ vidyate bhayam
english: For those who pay homage to Govinda, the imperishable one robed in yellow and resembling the flax-flower, no fear exists.

sanskrit: yathā viṣṇumayaṃ satyaṃ yathā viṣṇumayaṃ haviḥ yathā viṣṇumayaṃ sarvaṃ pāpmā me naśyatāṃ tathā
english: As truth is pervaded by Viṣṇu, as the oblation is pervaded by Viṣṇu, as all is pervaded by Viṣṇu—so let my sin be destroyed.

sanskrit: tvāṃ prapannāya bhaktāya gatim iṣṭāṃ jigīṣave yac chreyaḥ puṇḍarīkākṣa tad dhyāyasva surottama
english: For the devotee who has taken refuge in you and longs to win the goal he desires—meditate upon that which is his highest good, O lotus-eyed one, best of gods.

sanskrit: iti vidyātapoyonir ayonir viṣṇur īḍitaḥ vāgyajñenārcito devaḥ prīyatāṃ me janārdanaḥ
english: Thus is Viṣṇu praised, the womb of knowledge and austerity yet himself unborn; worshipped with the sacrifice of speech, may the god Janārdana be gracious to me.

sanskrit: etāvad uktvā vacanaṃ bhīṣmas tadgatamānasaḥ nama ity eva kṛṣṇāya praṇāmam akarot tadā
english: Having spoken this much, his mind wholly fixed upon him, Bhīṣma then made obeisance to Kṛṣṇa with the single word "Homage."

sanskrit: abhigamya tu yogena bhaktiṃ bhīṣmasya mādhavaḥ traikālyadarśanaṃ jñānaṃ divyaṃ dātuṃ yayau hariḥ
english: And Mādhava, having through his yogic power perceived Bhīṣma's devotion, departed—Hari going to bestow the divine knowledge that beholds the three times.

sanskrit: tasminn uparate śabde tatas te brahmavādinaḥ bhīṣmaṃ vāgbhir bāṣpakaṇṭhās tam ānarcur mahāmatim
english: When that utterance had ceased, those expounders of the sacred word, their throats choked with tears, then honored the great-minded Bhīṣma with their words.

sanskrit: te stuvantaś ca viprāgryāḥ keśavaṃ puruṣottamam bhīṣmaṃ ca śanakaiḥ sarve praśaśaṃsuḥ punaḥ punaḥ
english: And those foremost of brahmins, praising Keśava, the supreme Person, all softly extolled Bhīṣma as well, again and again.

sanskrit: viditvā bhaktiyogaṃ tu bhīṣmasya puruṣottamaḥ sahasotthāya saṃhṛṣṭo yānam evānvapadyata
english: And the supreme Person, having recognized Bhīṣma's devout discipline, rose at once with delight and mounted his chariot.

sanskrit: keśavaḥ sātyakiś caiva rathenaikena jagmatuḥ apareṇa mahātmānau yudhiṣṭhiradhanaṃjayau
english: Keśava and Sātyaki went in one chariot; in another rode the two great-souled ones, Yudhiṣṭhira and Dhanaṃjaya.

sanskrit: bhīmaseno yamau cobhau ratham ekaṃ samāsthitau kṛpo yuyutsuḥ sūtaś ca saṃjayaś cāparaṃ ratham
english: Bhīmasena and the twins together mounted one chariot, while Kṛpa, Yuyutsu, and the charioteer Saṃjaya took another.

sanskrit: te rathair nagarākāraiḥ prayātāḥ puruṣarṣabhāḥ nemighoṣeṇa mahatā kampayanto vasuṃdharām
english: Those bulls among men set forth in chariots vast as cities, making the earth tremble with the mighty thunder of their wheel-rims.

sanskrit: tato giraḥ puruṣavaras tavānvitā; dvijeritāḥ pathi sumanāḥ sa śuśruve kṛtāñjaliṃ praṇatam athāparaṃ janaṃ; sa keśihā muditamanābhyanandata
english: Then that best of men, glad of heart, heard along the way the words uttered by the brahmins in your favor; and the slayer of Keśin, with gladdened mind, greeted in return the other folk who bowed before him with joined palms.

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca tataḥ sa ca hṛṣīkeśaḥ sa ca rājā yudhiṣṭhiraḥ kṛpādayaś ca te sarve catvāraḥ pāṇḍavāś ca ha
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: Then Hṛṣīkeśa, and King Yudhiṣṭhira, and Kṛpa and all the rest, and the four Pāṇḍavas as well—

sanskrit: rathais te nagarākāraiḥ patākādhvajaśobhitaiḥ yayur āśu kurukṣetraṃ vājibhiḥ śīghragāmibhiḥ
english: in their chariots vast as cities, splendid with pennants and banners, swiftly went to Kurukṣetra, drawn by fleet-footed horses.

sanskrit: te 'vatīrya kurukṣetraṃ keśamajjāsthisaṃkulam dehanyāsaḥ kṛto yatra kṣatriyais tair mahātmabhiḥ
english: They came down upon Kurukṣetra, thick with hair, marrow, and bones, where those great-souled warriors had laid down their bodies—

sanskrit: gajāśvadehāsthicayaiḥ parvatair iva saṃcitam naraśīrṣakapālaiś ca śaṅkhair iva samācitam
english: heaped as if with mountains formed of the bodies and bones of elephants and horses, and strewn with men's skulls like conch-shells.

sanskrit: citāsahasrair nicitaṃ varmaśastrasamākulam āpānabhūmiṃ kālasya tadā bhuktojjhitām iva
english: Covered with thousands of funeral pyres, cluttered with armor and weapons, it was like a banqueting-ground of Death, just then feasted upon and cast aside.

sanskrit: bhūtasaṃghānucaritaṃ rakṣogaṇaniṣevitam paśyantas te kurukṣetraṃ yayur āśu mahārathāḥ
english: Beholding Kurukṣetra, roamed by hosts of spirits and frequented by troops of rākṣasas, those great chariot-warriors swiftly went on.

sanskrit: gacchann eva mahābāhuḥ sarvayādavanandanaḥ yudhiṣṭhirāya provāca jāmadagnyasya vikramam
english: As he went, the mighty-armed delight of all the Yādavas spoke to Yudhiṣṭhira of the valor of the son of Jamadagni.

sanskrit: amī rāmahradāḥ pañca dṛśyante pārtha dūrataḥ yeṣu saṃtarpayām āsa pūrvān kṣatriyaśoṇitaiḥ
english: "Yonder, O Pārtha, seen from afar, are those five lakes of Rāma, in which he satisfied the ancestors with the blood of the warriors.

sanskrit: triḥsaptakṛtvo vasudhāṃ kṛtvā niḥkṣatriyāṃ prabhuḥ ihedānīṃ tato rāmaḥ karmaṇo virarāma ha
english: Having thrice-seven times made the earth free of warriors, the lord Rāma then desisted here from that deed."

sanskrit: yudhiṣṭhira uvāca triḥsaptakṛtvaḥ pṛthivī kṛtā niḥkṣatriyā tadā rāmeṇeti yad āttha tvam atra me saṃśayo mahān
english: Yudhiṣṭhira said: "In that you tell me the earth was then made thrice-seven times free of warriors by Rāma—herein lies a great doubt of mine.

sanskrit: kṣatrabījaṃ yadā dagdhaṃ rāmeṇa yadupuṃgava kathaṃ bhūyaḥ samutpattiḥ kṣatrasyāmitavikrama
english: When the seed of the warrior race had been burned away by Rāma, O bull of the Yadus, how came the warrior race once more into being, O you of boundless valor?

sanskrit: mahātmanā bhagavatā rāmeṇa yadupuṃgava katham utsāditaṃ kṣatraṃ kathaṃ vṛddhiṃ punar gatam
english: How was the warrior race rooted out by the great-souled, venerable Rāma, O bull of the Yadus, and how did it again attain increase?"

sanskrit: mahābhāratayuddhe hi koṭiśaḥ kṣatriyā hatāḥ tathābhūc ca mahī kīrṇā kṣatriyair vadatāṃ vara
english: "For in the great Bhārata war warriors were slain by the millions, and the earth thus came to be strewn with warriors, O best of speakers.

sanskrit: evaṃ me chindhi vārṣṇeya saṃśayaṃ tārkṣyaketana āgamo hi paraḥ kṛṣṇa tvatto no vāsavānuja
english: Sever this doubt of mine thus, O scion of Vṛṣṇi, you whose banner bears Garuḍa; for from you, Kṛṣṇa, younger brother of Vāsava, comes our highest authority."

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca tato vrajann eva gadāgrajaḥ prabhuḥ; śaśaṃsa tasmai nikhilena tattvataḥ yudhiṣṭhirāyāpratimaujase tadā; yathābhavat kṣatriyasaṃkulā mahī
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: Then, even as he journeyed on, the lord, elder brother of Gada, recounted to him in full and truly—to Yudhiṣṭhira of matchless might—how it was that the earth came to be thronged with warriors.

sanskrit: vāsudeva uvāca śṛṇu kaunteya rāmasya mayā yāvat pariśrutam maharṣīṇāṃ kathayatāṃ kāraṇaṃ tasya janma ca
english: Vāsudeva said: Hear, O son of Kuntī, so much of Rāma as I have heard from the great seers as they told the cause of it and of his birth.

sanskrit: yathā ca jāmadagnyena koṭiśaḥ kṣatriyā hatāḥ udbhūtā rājavaṃśeṣu ye bhūyo bhārate hatāḥ
english: and how warriors were slain by the millions by the son of Jamadagni—those who, having sprung up again in the royal lines, were slain once more in the Bhārata war.

sanskrit: jahnor ajahnus tanayo ballavas tasya cātmajaḥ kuśiko nāma dharmajñas tasya putro mahīpatiḥ
english: Jahnu's son was Ajahnu, and his son was Ballava; his son was the law-knowing king named Kuśika.

sanskrit: ugraṃ tapaḥ samātiṣṭhat sahasrākṣasamo bhuvi putraṃ labheyam ajitaṃ trilokeśvaram ity uta
english: On earth, the peer of the thousand-eyed god, he undertook fierce austerity, with the wish: "May I obtain a son unconquered, a lord of the three worlds."

sanskrit: tam ugratapasaṃ dṛṣṭvā sahasrākṣaḥ puraṃdaraḥ samarthaḥ putrajanane svayam evaitya bhārata
english: Seeing him fierce in austerity, the thousand-eyed Purandara, able himself to be begotten as a son, came in person, O Bhārata.

sanskrit: putratvam agamad rājaṃs tasya lokeśvareśvaraḥ gādhir nāmābhavat putraḥ kauśikaḥ pākaśāsanaḥ
english: That lord over the lords of the worlds attained sonship to him, O king; the son who was born, named Gādhi, descended of Kuśika, was the chastiser of Pāka.

sanskrit: tasya kanyābhavad rājan nāmnā satyavatī prabho tāṃ gādhiḥ kaviputrāya sorcīkāya dadau prabhuḥ
english: To him was born a daughter named Satyavatī, O sovereign king; and the lord Gādhi gave her to Ṛcīka, son of the sage Aurva.

sanskrit: tataḥ prītas tu kaunteya bhārgavaḥ kurunandana putrārthe śrapayām āsa caruṃ gādhes tathaiva ca
english: Then well pleased, O son of Kuntī, delight of the Kurus, the descendant of Bhṛgu cooked a sacrificial porridge for the sake of a son, and one likewise for Gādhi.

sanskrit: āhūya cāha tāṃ bhāryām ṛcīko bhārgavas tadā upayojyaś carur ayaṃ tvayā mātrāpy ayaṃ tava
english: And summoning his wife, Ṛcīka of the line of Bhṛgu then said: "This porridge is to be consumed by you, and this one by your mother.

sanskrit: tasyā janiṣyate putro dīptimān kṣatriyarṣabhaḥ ajayyaḥ kṣatriyair loke kṣatriyarṣabhasūdanaḥ
english: To her will be born a radiant son, a bull among warriors, unconquerable by warriors in the world, a slayer of the bulls among warriors.

sanskrit: tavāpi putraṃ kalyāṇi dhṛtimantaṃ taponvitam śamātmakaṃ dvijaśreṣṭhaṃ carur eṣa vidhāsyati
english: And for you too, fair lady, this porridge will ordain a son, steadfast, endowed with austerity, of tranquil nature, the foremost of the twice-born."

sanskrit: ity evam uktvā tāṃ bhāryām ṛcīko bhṛgunandanaḥ tapasy abhirato dhīmāñ jagāmāraṇyam eva ha
english: Having spoken thus to his wife, Ṛcīka, the delight of the Bhṛgus, wise and devoted to austerity, went away into the forest.

sanskrit: etasminn eva kāle tu tīrthayātrāparo nṛpaḥ gādhiḥ sadāraḥ saṃprāpta ṛcīkasyāśramaṃ prati
english: At this very time King Gādhi, bent on a pilgrimage to the holy fords, arrived together with his wife at the hermitage of Ṛcīka.

sanskrit: carudvayaṃ gṛhītvā tu rājan satyavatī tadā bhartur vākyād athāvyagrā mātre hṛṣṭā nyavedayat
english: Taking up the two portions of porridge, O king, Satyavatī then, calm and following her husband's word, gladly presented them to her mother.

sanskrit: mātā tu tasyāḥ kaunteya duhitre svaṃ caruṃ dadau tasyāś carum athājñātam ātmasaṃsthaṃ cakāra ha
english: But her mother, O son of Kuntī, gave her own portion to her daughter, and unknowingly took her daughter's portion for herself.
